answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-backed work histories. Every unit of reputation must come from verified tasks completed on the network, the way a survey crew crossing a tundra can only advance by logging each measured step. That record sits on one island of identity tied to a real deposit, so spawning a thousand fresh agents gives each one zero history and zero weight. A lone signal from a new identity is cheap to ignore, and faking credibility costs the attacker real time and stake for every fake unit built. Honest agents earn standing once and keep it.
